samples.summary: Prototype-reachable object-literal lookups still feed OOXML attributes, contradicting this file's own "closed lookup" claim
samples.evidence: The change fixes exactly this pattern in two places (`ALGN` and `UNDERLINE_STYLE_TO_U` become `Map`s, `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` is a `Map`) and the comment at color.ts:24-31 asserts "every attribute this function emits is either [0-9A-F]{6}, a closed ROLE_TO_SCHEME value, or a finite number". `ROLE_TO_SCHEME` is a plain object literal, so `ROLE_TO_SCHEME[c.role]` at color.ts:49 consults `Object.prototype`: a persisted `{kind:'role', role:'constructor'}` yields `function Object() { [native code] }` and `role:'__proto__'` yields `[object Object]`, both stringified straight into `<a:schemeClr val="...">`. `colorChildXml` has no unknown-role fallback at all (`val="undefined"`), even though the design doc added by this change claims one. `storedColorToThemeColor` (text.ts:212) validates the role, but the fill/gradient/effect callers do not — `fillXml`/`gradFillXml` (color.ts:77, 93) and `effects.ts:22` take colors straight off slide-element JSON, which the content PUT API only validates for `id`/`type`/`frame` (docs-content.controller.ts:500-520). Same unfixed pattern at shape.ts:63 (`DASH_VAL[stroke.dash]`), connector.ts:55-56 (`KIND_TO_OOXML[a.kind]`, `SIZE_TO_OOXML[a.size]`) and layout.ts:53 (`BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE[layout.id]`). I could not construct an actual XML injection: no `Object.prototype` member stringifies to a value containing `"`, `<`, `>` or `&`, so the impact is an attacker-chosen, schema-invalid attribute rather than element injection — hence minor, not critical.
searchedFor: grep for `^const [A-Z_]+ = {` lookup tables in packages/slides/src/export
read colorChildXml, storedColorToThemeColor, effects.ts call site

samples.summary: The new block-style allowlist covers only the docs arm of the endpoint; the slides arm persists the same block shapes with no value validation
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` (alignment allowlist + finite-number geometry) is reached only from `assertValidBlock`, which is called only from `assertValidDocsBody` (line 250) and `assertValidHeaderFooter` (line 285). The same controller's slides arm, `assertValidSlidesBody` → `assertValidSlide` → `assertValidElement` (lines 428-520), validates only `id`, `type` and `frame` — a slide text-box `textBody.blocks[*].style.alignment`, `listLevel`, `marker.color` and `inline.style.color` are written verbatim by `writeSlidesRoot` and later reach the PPTX attribute sinks. Those sinks now normalize (`ALGN` Map, `listLevelAttr`, `toRgbHexColor`), so this is defence-in-depth coverage only, not a live bypass — but the added guard reads as a payload-wide guarantee it does not have, which is precisely the failure mode the change's own lessons doc describes.
searchedFor: grep assertValidBlock / assertValidBlockStyle call sites in packages/backend/src
grep writeDocsRoot call sites in packages/backend/src (single call site, no bypass)

samples.summary: Unvalidated inline `style.image` / `tableData.rowHeights` still crash the writer: authenticated 500 instead of the 400 this validator exists to give
samples.evidence: The new inline validation (controller lines 401-418) checks `text` and `style` but nothing inside `style`. `serializeInlineStyle` then does `if (style.image !== undefined) { attrs['image.src'] = style.image.src; ... }` (docs-tree.ts:89-95), so a PUT body of `{"blocks":[{"id":"a","type":"paragraph","style":{},"inlines":[{"text":"x","style":{"image":null}}]}]}` dereferences `null.src` inside `doc.update` → TypeError → HTTP 500 from inside Yorkie. Same class at docs-tree.ts:267-271: `block.tableData.rowHeights` is unvalidated, so `"rowHeights":"abc"` reaches `.map` on a string → TypeError. Impact is limited to a 500 for a workspace-authorized caller (no data exposure), so minor, but it is the exact unvalidated-input-reaches-writer class the diff set out to close.
searchedFor: read assertValidBlock inline loop in docs-content.controller.ts
read serializeInlineStyle / buildBlockNode in backend docs-tree.ts

samples.summary: `<w:pStyle w:val="Heading${headingLevel}"/>` interpolates an untrusted model field raw, two lines above the alignment sink this change hardened
samples.evidence: `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` now routes `style.alignment` through the closed `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` map (line 144) on the stated grounds that "the value reaching an exporter is whatever string was persisted into the CRDT", but its sibling attribute on line 135 still interpolates `headingLevel` with no coercion — a value like `1"/><w:jc w:val="right` would be written verbatim into document.xml / header1.xml. I could not complete the exploit chain: both CRDT readers coerce it (`Number(attrs.headingLevel)` at backend docs-tree.ts:460 and frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:507), so via the content PUT API the value is a number (possibly NaN) by the time any export runs. The gap is only reachable by an export path that consumes model JSON without a CRDT round-trip; hence low confidence, but the raw interpolation is the defect.
searchedFor: grep headingLevel across packages (readers, importers, clipboard HEADING_MAP)
read backend docs-tree.ts treeNodeToBlock, frontend yorkie-doc-store parseBlock
checked other raw attribute interpolations in docx-exporter.ts (colSpan/rowSpan/twips are numerically coerced)

samples.summary: No depth bound on the recursive block validator/writer — deeply nested tableData can exhaust the stack
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlock` recurses into `tableData.rows[*].cells[*].blocks[*]` (line 377) and `buildBlockNode`/`buildCellNode` recurse the same way (docs-tree.ts:259-301), with no nesting limit anywhere on the path. A body with a few thousand nested table blocks — cheap to generate and well within a normal JSON body limit — produces a RangeError inside the request. Impact is a 500 per request for an authorized caller rather than a process kill (Nest catches it), so minor; I did not measure the actual depth threshold or the configured body-size limit, hence low confidence.
searchedFor: read assertValidBlock / assertValidHeaderFooter recursion in docs-content.controller.ts
read buildBlockNode / buildCellNode recursion in backend docs-tree.ts
grep for any depth/limit constant in the controller and docs-tree

finding.summary: PPTX color modifier attributes (`alpha`, `tint`, `shade`, `lumMod`, `lumOff`) are still interpolated raw after this change removed the file's only XML escaping
finding.evidence:
This diff deletes `import { escapeXmlAttr } from './xml.js'` from `color.ts` and replaces the escaped hex with `toRgbHexColor(c.value) ?? '000000'`, on the stated theory that normalization subsumes escaping. But lines 25-29 of the same function still do `mods.push(`<a:lumMod val="${c.lumMod}"/>`)` … `<a:alpha val="${c.alpha}"/>` with no coercion, and after this change nothing in the file escapes anything.

Vector: those fields are typed `number` but are *persisted JSON*. `packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:101-104` assigns `root.slides = document.slides` verbatim, and `assertValidElement` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:393-413) validates only `id`, `type` and `frame` — element `fill`/`stroke`/`effects` colors are never inspected. An authenticated workspace member (or an API key) PUTs an element whose fill is `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '#ffffff', alpha: '0"/><a:hlinkClick r:id="rId2' }`. When any user later exports the deck, `fillXml → solidFillXml → colorChildXml` emits `<a:alpha val="0"/><a:hlinkClick r:id="rId2"/>` — attacker-chosen OOXML elements inside the generated slide part.

The same sink is reachable from the function this diff actually rewrote: `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:213-216` copies `out.tint = c.tint; out.shade = c.shade` straight off an untrusted docs `StoredColor` role object, so `{ kind:'role', role:'accent1', tint:'1"/><a:alpha val="0' }` on an inline style reaches `<a:tint val=…>` unescaped even though the srgb arm right above it is now normalized.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the color modifier attributes (alpha/tint/shade/lumMod/lumOff) are still raw-interpolated in color.ts after escaping was removed. That code is not present in the repository. All five modifiers are emitted through modifierXml (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:33-38), which does `const n = Number(value); if (!Number.isFinite(n)) return '';` and interpolates the coerced number `n`, not the original value. The claimed payload `alpha: '0"/><a:hlinkClick r:id="rId2'` coerces to NaN and the modifier is dropped, so no attacker text reaches the XML. The raw `mods.push(`<a:lumMod val="${c.lumMod}"/>`)` form the reviewer quoted exists only in an archived design doc (docs/tasks/archive/2026/06/20260623-slides-pptx-export-todo.md:437-441), not in the source file; the cited lines 25-29 of color.ts are the doc comment explaining the coercion. An existing test (packages/slides/test/export/pptx/color.test.ts:112-126) exercises the exact injection payload and asserts the modifier is dropped. The text.ts sub-claim also fails: text.ts:214-215 copies tint/shade uncoerced, but its only sink is colorChildXml, which coerces at lines 44-45, and the role value is validated against ROLE_TO_SCHEME keys at text.ts:212 with a black fallback at text.ts:219. The srgb `val` is normalized via toRgbHexColor(...) ?? '000000' (color.ts:59) and gradFillXml emits only arithmetic-derived integers (color.ts:76,81), so no unescaped attacker-controlled attribute sink remains in the file.

finding.summary: The new API-side alignment allowlist never runs on header/footer blocks (or on slides text-body blocks), so the same value it rejects can still be persisted through the same endpoint
finding.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` is only reached from `assertValidBlock`, and `assertValidDocsBody` (controller.ts:249-251) walks only `body.blocks`. But `writeDocsRoot` also persists `document.header.blocks` and `document.footer.blocks` (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:289-303`, each child built with the same `buildBlockNode`, whose `serializeBlockStyle` writes `alignment: style.alignment` verbatim at `:143`). So `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:ws/documents/:id/content` with `{"blocks":[],"header":{"marginFromEdge":0,"blocks":[{"id":"b1","type":"paragraph","style":{"alignment":"center\"/><w:jc w:val=\"right"},"inlines":[]}]}}` bypasses the gate entirely, and the value flows to the *same* sink via `DocxExporter.buildHeaderFooterXml` → `blockToXml` → `buildParagraphPropertiesXml`, landing in `word/header1.xml`. The identical hole exists on the slides arm: `assertValidSlidesBody`/`assertValidElement` (controller.ts:415-435) check only `id`/`type`/`frame`, so element text-body blocks carry arbitrary `style.alignment` into `ALGN[...]` in the PPTX exporter. Header/footer blocks also skip every other block check (`id`, `type`, `style`, `inlines`), so a malformed block reaches `buildBlockNode` unguarded. Exploitability of the alignment payload is currently blocked by the exporter-side lookup — but that lookup has the prototype-chain hole reported separately, and the guard reads as covering a sink it does not cover. Fix: run `assertValidBlock` over `body.header?.blocks` / `body.footer?.blocks` (and over slides element text bodies).

verdict.reason: The finding claims the alignment allowlist never runs on header/footer blocks, but assertValidDocsBody explicitly validates both regions. docs-content.controller.ts:258-259 calls assertValidHeaderFooter(body.header,'header') and assertValidHeaderFooter(body.footer,'footer') right after the body.blocks loop; that helper (262-287) validates marginFromEdge (275-283) and runs every region block through the same assertValidBlock walker (284-286), which enforces id (341), type (344), style-is-object (347) and calls assertValidBlockStyle (350) whose BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS allowlist (289, 314-322) rejects the reviewer's exact payload. Tests assert this: docs-content.controller.spec.ts:565-601 cover a bad header alignment, a bad footer block id, and a non-finite header.marginFromEdge. The secondary slides sub-claim also does not reach a sink: packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:69-74 defines ALGN as a Map and :99 uses ALGN.get(...) ?? 'l', and packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:118-123/:144 likewise uses a Map, so the prototype-chain escape the finding depends on does not exist; unvalidated slides text-body alignment is at most non-blocking hardening.
